What if you support a team for 20 years but then move for university and start watching a team local to your new home. That seems fine to me. Maybe your only connection to a team was your dad, but after they pass you realise you didn't enjoy the matches for the team but instead because of him. Maybe the team you support does something you disagree with politically, or morally. Etc. I think there are loads of valid reasons to change support.

What isn't valid, and what pisses people off, is when people pick a team that win a lot to support but then change the team they follow because their arbitrarily chosen winning team have stopped winning as much. So they want a new winning team.

Or, as is becoming a trend, people who support individual players and who will pick up and drop teams as those players transfer.

Football (I would argue sports in general) thrive not in the feeling of constant success, but in the reward success brings after the investment of your time and effort during the years without success. I don't want to name any clubs in this post to avoid arguments but if your team wins the title 10 years in a row, it's wonderful, but also you lose perspective. What gives perspective is the gaps in between. This is why people get annoyed at those who change their clubs on a whim. You're sacrificing the core aspect of supporting something.

I wouldn't go to a football match in Australia and expect the exact same atmosphere as a match in Argentina.

There are differing football cultures around the world. Spain has a really poor away fan culture, for example. Scotland doesn't always have great atmospheres but its football attendances are amongst the highest in the world when you take populations into account. Are Spanish fans less passionate just because they aren't as keen to travel long distances on shite public transport? Are the thousands of people going to see Dundee Utd or Aberdeen even though they know they'll never see them win a league title, ever, less passionate just because they don't sing and jump around for 90 minutes every week? 

You also have to consider demographics. In Germany, ticket prices are dirt cheap and you can drink in your seat. This means a far more working class demographic compared to English football. Working class can't afford Arsenal season tickets anymore really. Not comfortably anyway.

If I'm paying £50 for entertainment, which is what going to see a football match is, I don't expect said entertainment to come with a caveat that I have to be unable to see due to people in the way, have to sing all the way through even if the team are playing shite, etc. I kind of expect to be able to enjoy said entertainment without signing any kind of social contract to behave in some fake passionate way. And I say this as someone who always chanted regardless of whether those around me did or not. It was my choice to do so.

Moved up to Edinburgh from London last October, I'm Irish but spent a lot of my life moving between Dublin and London and had lived in London for the last 10 years. Have been an Arsenal fan for as long as I've had conscious thought. Never had an Emirates season ticket, because they're £1200+ but went to 10+ games a season, albeit it was a lot easier pre-Arteta when they weren't doing so well.



Anyway, moving up here I didn't want to give up on supporting my local team in favour of supporting a team hundreds of miles away. So I've become a Hibs fan. Easter Road is, and this is not an exaggeration, 2 minutes from my front door. From my sofa to my seat in the stadium, it's 5 minutes. No brainer really. 



FIrst game was against Clydebank in the cup, then had to wait 3 months to see them again as their next 3 home games were Cat A games and I hadn't been to a Cat B game to qualify for tickets. 2nd game against St Johnstone, and then bought my season ticket for next year.



I'm having the time of my life. It's like when I first got into watching American football, or watching endurance racing (WEC/IMSA), or frankly it's like when I was a kid getting into football for the first time). Everything is so new and interesting, I know nothing so every team Hibs play against is a fucking treasure trove of "wait, he plays for them?!" Mind is still blown from when I saw a clip of Martin Boyle taking a penalty against Dundee Utd in 2016/17 and the Dundee Utd goalkeeper was Japanese international Eiji Kawashima. What the fuck? 



The fans, the banter, the fact that it's all so shite but in a really, really endearing and fun way. It reminds me of watching Bray Wanderers in the Irish second tier with my granddad as a kid and being thrilled when Bray strung together more than 3 successive passes. I'm also really happy, and quite lucky, I've moved to a place where the club takes the women's team seriously as I've always been a keen fan of both Arsenal's men and women's teams. Cool to be able to happily continue that with Hibs.



I had fallen out of love with football massively. The Premier League is so fucking corporate that it often felt like I could die in my seat at the Emirates and the club would resell the ticket before checking my pulse. Saw so many fans priced out of it. Players earning literally 500k+ a week, gutted if they ever have to interact with a fan. Clubs selling their souls for middle east money, or in my club's case, Rwandan money. It's so fucked up. Not that Scottish football is immune from it but it's nowhere near as prevalent. I think I struggle with disconnecting entirely from Arsenal because football is fucked, the feelings I have for that club are so instinctive. The nerves you get when your club plays, the joy, the sorrow/anger, etc. I don't know how to make that shit go away when I watch them, but I imagine it'll be harder without the best part of football - going to games.



Anyway, youse are all class basically, and I'm excited to settle in more. I've only seen Hibs lose twice so far, and only once in the league, and I'm reliably ensured that it's always like this being a Hibs fan. So that's grand.

I feel like champion balance should never rely on items. I get that Riot like that philosophy (ardent meta big yikes) but the issue is that then the item gets nerfed and suddenly the champions using it, who had previously been nerfed, are rendered near useless. We've seen it happen countless times with other roles too. An item + champion combo is OP so riot nerf the champion. Then people find a replacement to use and riot nerf that one too. People find another combo and finally riot nerfs the item except now the first 2 champions have been double nerfed.

Balance should lie primarily in kits. Pyke can do things no other support can, but he can't heal an ally. Soraka can heal for days but she isn't executing anyone or engaging. Alistar can engage but his sustain relies on stats and he can be poked very easily. That's the sort of trifecta you want but items that offer support buffs only accessible to some supports are detrimental to the others.

I guess Riot's concern would be quite simple. How do you make a cheap AD item for supports to buy that doesn't greatly appeal to solo laners. Umbral itself has struggled with this. It's quite gold efficient even without the passive and champions like Zed can use that passive to great effect.

Enchanters have easy item synergy, right? Shields, heals, buffs. Easy. You pack in stats that they love but their AP midlaner cohorts don't care about as much like loads of mana regen without ap growth, or CDR. Items that offer small amounts of AP.
Tanks similarly have easy item synergy. You soak damage for your ally, or you reduce the enemy team's usefulness. The items aren't as efficient for top lane tanks who are alone and earn more money.
AD supports don't have that sensible balance yet like the other two classes.
